title: Bunk teaching in Mandeville; Tommy Ladner and Cliff Bass
summary: The Mandeville hall, Bunk living and teaching a band there, trumpeter Tommy Ladner, and drummer Cliff Bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Is that right where they had a boat in those days, didn't they? Yeah.
A boat. A boat.
And when was it you played then? Mandeville. I mean, what kind of a hall was it? Right at the ferry place?
Yeah, yeah.
Right on the shore then?
Right. It was about four blocks on the center side. Not all up that floor, but two blocks or three blocks. That's where I met Bunk before he got playing here.
Is that right? I know Bunk was over there for a while.
Bunk used to stay over there.
Yeah. In Mandeville.
Yeah, he used to stay over there. I know he used to teach the band. A whole lot of, he learned a whole lot of fellas. Band. Yeah. He had a good band, too.

I know Tommy Ladner, he said, learned from him over there in the band. Yeah. Did you know Tommy Ladner? He left here when he was real young. I guess you didn't know him much. Went to Chicago and played a lot up there. Where did he play?
Trumpet.
Oh, kind of a light fella.
Yeah. Well, he was a light fella. Yeah, yeah. I know him. He was a light fella. He was a little old. I know him.
I see him play.
He was a small fella.
Yeah. He worked in Chicago a lot, then went to New York. But I guess he didn't play much here at all.

No. But Uncle Lonnie taught a lot of fellas around here. They had a good band on that lick there, too. You know what I'm saying? It looked like they didn't know nothing but sure he'd get to play in there. Cliff Bass, the drummer he did. He died not so long ago. That was a drummer. Look at that fella.
What was his name?
Cliff Bass. I forgot his last name. He's brother. He's got a brother, Frank Connick. That bright fella.
